items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: I mean I was a second engineer on a lot of Duke Ellington dates and boy they flew.

ctx.x: What is your opinion, you’re driving down the street these days, the music that you hear coming out of some cars is very different from what you would have heard coming out of cars in the 1960s.

You bet. I think that we worked a lot better in the 60s. I mean we were, you know, our equipment has gotten better since the 60s but I don’t think that, you know music doesn’t change. Music is music. And whether you do a date with Duke Ellington in 1960 or you do a date with Duke Ellington now, the music is still there. You’ve just got to make it better. I mean I was a second engineer on a lot of Duke Ellington dates and boy they flew. You know you had to be real quick. You could turn around and say, “Give me…
What possessed you to try to get the members of the Monkees to play their own instruments?
